why: I read the statement the way its link to 'Measure-preserving dynamical system' and the specialist literature (Kanigowski-Lemanczyk 2020, Ryzhikov 2024) read it: an ergodic, probability-preserving Z-action whose Koopman operator on mean-zero L2 has simple Lebesgue spectrum. On that reading, each pre-snapshot affirmative result is a changed question (variant): sigma-finite measure (El Abdalaoui 2015/2022), flows or R^d actions (Prikhod'ko 2010/2011/2020, El Abdalaoui 2020), non-singular maps (2014). Multiplicity-two and infinite-multiplicity results are also variants. Negative results about particular constructions, and surveys, are scope none. The OpenAI manuscript claims exactly this probability-preserving Z-action, as an existence theorem: a C^inf volume-preserving diffeomorphism of T^3 with a cyclic vector whose orbit is an orthonormal basis of L2_0. That answers the existence question in full if it is correct, so the scope is whole. The limit map is non-explicit, so it is not checkable; nobody has reviewed it, the Lean main theorem was seen as 'by sorry', so it is unreviewed. It is credible, because no specific error has been identified and only 8 days have passed. The object is a witness. The AI role is generated on the README's procedure statement, and the family is not among the named exceptions. The two OpenAI entries describe one release; I scored them identically.
doubts: Close call on scope: the bullet does not fix the measure or the time group. If a sigma-finite or flow system counts, El Abdalaoui 2015 or Prikhod'ko 2020 (journal-published) would already answer the bullet before the snapshot. I chose the probability-preserving Z-action reading, following the link target and the specialist surveys. The AI credit rests on the README's general statement; the manuscript's own credit sentence was not read. The two OpenAI events duplicate one release.
